//: Composite indexes. Firestore serves single-field equality, a lone orderBy, and equality on one field automatically; a composite index is required for two or more equality filters, or an equality/range filter combined with an orderBy on a different field. Every query in src/lib/api.js and functions/index.js was audited against that rule -- see README 'Query and index audit' for the full table.

indexes.//: setPrice: pricesRef.where('fuelType','==',x).where('effectiveTo','==',null) -- two equality filters, so this one genuinely needs a composite index. Without it, closing the previous price interval fails and a price change would leave two open intervals for the same fuel.

getPrices orders the whole subcollection by effectiveFrom desc. A lone orderBy is covered by the automatic single-field index; this entry exists so the descending direction is explicit and survives any future addition of an equality filter on fuelType.
